name: conversion-graph
title: Conversion graph
tagline: straight-line unit-conversion graph on a numbered grid; line from a rate or two points; dashed read-off guides with derived, occludable values, or arm read-off to read one off.
description: A straight-line conversion graph between two units on a numbered grid with unit-labelled axes — the classic "use the graph to convert X" read-off figure (miles↔kilometres, pounds↔dollars, litres↔pints, °C↔°F). You give the two axis labels (with units) and ranges, and the line as EITHER a rate (y = rate·x, a line through the origin) OR two points (the gradient and intercept are derived, for an offset line such as °C↔°F). The model draws the line clipped to the window and derives every read-off: a read-off gives a value on one axis and a direction (from the x-axis or the y-axis), and the model draws the dashed guide L-shape up/across to the line and back to the other axis, marks the meeting point, and computes the converted value on the destination axis — which you can occlude as "?" for a "use the graph to convert…" question or highlight as the answer. Read-offs work in BOTH directions on the same graph. Extra scaffold points can be plotted for a "the line passes through … , draw it" answer space. ANSWER ON THE MODEL (@2, responseMode "read-off"): give readOff { from, value } (singular — the given amount, public) and the figure becomes a "use the graph to read off a value" answer surface: the line is SHOWN and the pupil drags the dashed construction line from the given value to the line and back to the other axis; the endpoint self-checks against the DERIVED converted value within a tolerance ({ derived: true } sentinel, never drawn on a posed surface). The static readOffs (plural) stay the worked/occluded teaching guide.
whenToUse: Reach for this for any straight-line unit-conversion graph and the "use the graph to convert…" read-off: miles↔kilometres, pounds↔dollars (or any currency), litres↔pints/gallons, kilograms↔pounds, inches↔centimetres, and the offset °C↔°F line. Give axes.x and axes.y each a label (INCLUDING the unit, e.g. "Distance (miles)" or just "Miles"), a range [min,max] and optionally a step (grid spacing) and labelStep (how often to number). Define the line ONE of two ways: line.rate for a line through the origin (rate = how many y-units per x-unit — e.g. rate 1.6 for miles→km, rate 1.75 for litres→pints), OR line.points as two [x,y] anchor pairs for a line that may not pass through the origin (the offset °C↔°F line is line.points [[0,32],[100,212]]; a through-origin line can also be given this way, e.g. [[0,0],[5,8]] for 5 miles = 8 km). Never author the plotted line's pixel coordinates — give the rate or the anchor points and the model derives the line. Add read-offs to pose or work "convert N units" tasks: readOffs [{ from: "x", value: 30 }] reads UP from 30 on the x-axis to the line and ACROSS to the y-axis (convert 30 x-units to y-units); from "y" reads across from the y-axis and DOWN to the x-axis (convert back). Set occlude:true on a read-off to hide the converted value as "?" (the question — the guides still draw so the pupil reads it off the graph); the input value always shows (it is the given). Read-offs default to the amber result colour (they ARE the answer); set highlight:false to keep one neutral. IMPORTANT — a read-off is only as precise as the gridlines: choose a step so the answer lands on or near a gridline, and when you key the answer in a question give a tolerance sized to the grid (roughly half a grid square), not the exact decimal. For a blank answer space ("draw the conversion line"), omit line (labelled axes only) and optionally plot the given anchor points with points. Common configurations: worked read-off — the line + one read-off shown with its value; question — the line + an occluded read-off + a caption; answer space — labelled axes, no line. Keep the same axes across the blocks of one lesson. ANSWER ON THE MODEL — "use the graph to read off …" (auto-marked, @2): a MARKED model tile with responseMode "read-off", marking { mode: "auto", correctAnswer: { derived: true } }, the line given, and readOff { from, value } (singular) naming the GIVEN axis + amount (NOT the static readOffs plural, which would draw the answer — that fails validation). The pupil drags the dashed construction line to the line and back to the other axis; the endpoint self-checks against the derived converted value within readOff.tolerance (default a quarter of the target axis step — half a small square; carry over the question's existing answer tolerance). A y-intercept read ("the fixed charge" / "the value at 0") is a read-off with from "x", value 0. Switch primitive when the teaching changes: for a curve y=f(x) use graphing/function-graph, for distance/speed–time use graphing/journey-graph, for the numeric single-step conversion as a ruler use number/double-number-line, for the metric ×10/÷10 staircase use number/metric-ladder. Synonyms a teacher might use: conversion graph, convert, unit conversion, read off, read-off, use the graph to, miles to km, kilometres, pounds to dollars, exchange rate, litres to pints, gallons, stones, kilograms, Celsius to Fahrenheit, temperature conversion, proportion line, straight-line graph.

axes.description: The two axes. x is the horizontal unit, y the vertical unit; the read-off converts between them.

label.description: Axis name, INCLUDING the unit, e.g. "Miles", "Distance (miles)", "Pounds (£)".

range.description: [min, max] in x-units, e.g. [0, 80]. May start below 0 (e.g. [-10, 40] for °C).

step.description: Grid spacing in x-units. Default: a sensible round value for the range. Choose it so read-off answers land on gridlines.

labelStep.description: Number the axis every this many units (a multiple of step) to keep wide ranges uncrowded. Default: every gridline.

label.description: Axis name, INCLUDING the unit, e.g. "Kilometres", "Dollars ($)".

range.description: [min, max] in y-units. Frame it so the line spans the plot.

step.description: Grid spacing in y-units. Default: a sensible round value.

labelStep.description: Number the axis every this many units. Default: every gridline.

line.description: The conversion line, given as SEMANTICS (never pixel coords). Provide EITHER rate (a line through the origin) OR points (two anchor pairs, for a line that may not pass through the origin). Omit the whole line for a blank answer space (labelled axes only).

rate.description: The conversion rate: y = rate · x, a line THROUGH THE ORIGIN. E.g. 1.6 for miles→km, 1.75 for litres→pints, 2.2 for kg→pounds. Use points instead for a line with a non-zero intercept.

points.description: Two [x, y] anchor points the line passes through; the gradient and intercept are derived. Use for an OFFSET line (°C↔°F is [[0,32],[100,212]]) or to give a through-origin line by its anchor pair ([[0,0],[5,8]] = 5 miles is 8 km). The two x-values must differ.

label.description: Optional short label drawn near the line (an equation or a name). Conversion lines are usually UNLABELLED — omit unless the equation is the point.

showLabel.description: Show the line label. Default false (conversion lines read as a bare line).

occlude.description: Hide the line label as "?" (for "what is the equation of this line?"). Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the line in the amber emphasis colour. Default false (the line is accent blue; amber is reserved for read-off results).

readOffs.description: Read-off guide constructions. Each takes a value on one axis and draws the dashed guide L-shape to the line and back to the other axis, computing the converted value. Read-offs work in both directions on the same graph.

from.description: "x" reads UP from value on the x-axis to the line, then ACROSS to the y-axis (convert an x-unit amount to y-units). "y" reads ACROSS from the y-axis to the line, then DOWN to the x-axis (convert back).

value.description: The GIVEN amount on the "from" axis (the question input). Always shown (it is not the answer). Must lie within that axis range.

occlude.description: Hide the converted value as "?" — the "use the graph to convert…" question hook. The guides still draw. Default false.

highlight.description: Draw the guides + converted value in amber (it is the result). Default TRUE. Set false to keep a read-off neutral (e.g. a second worked one).

label.description: Override the converted-value readout text (rarely needed). Omit to show the derived value.

readOff.description: The "use the graph to read off a value" ANSWER surface (@2, responseMode "read-off"). SINGULAR — the interactive answer twin of the static readOffs (plural). Names a GIVEN value on one axis; the line stays SHOWN and the pupil drags the dashed construction line to it and back to the OTHER axis (from x → UP then ACROSS; from y → ACROSS then DOWN). The endpoint self-checks against the DERIVED converted value within tolerance. The given value is public (it IS the question); the converted value is NEVER drawn on a posed / print surface. Do NOT also give the static readOffs (plural) on the same tile — that would draw the answer (leak).

from.description: "x" — the given value is on the x-axis; read UP to the line then ACROSS to the y-axis (convert an x-amount to y). "y" — the given value is on the y-axis; read ACROSS to the line then DOWN to the x-axis (convert back). A y-intercept read ("the value at 0") is from "x", value 0.

value.description: The GIVEN amount on the "from" axis (the question input — public, always marked). Must lie within that axis range and meet the line inside the window.

tolerance.description: Acceptance band on the TARGET (read) axis, in that axis's units. Default: a quarter of the target axis step (half a small square). Set it to carry over the question's existing answer tolerance.

points.description: Extra scaffold points to plot as marker dots — for a "the line passes through these points, draw the line" answer space. Each is an authored [x, y] with an optional label; not part of the line derivation.

occlude.description: Show the coordinate readout as "(?, ?)". Default false.

showGrid.description: Show background gridlines. Default true (pupils read off the grid).

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure.
